headline: FBI ARTEX AI attack tool now a 3-outlet story; Check Point and UnrealIRCd KEV deadlines hit 11-16; TSMC breach tied to cloud

bullets.text: Developing: the FBI warning that the ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering cyberattacks worldwide is now reported by 3 outlets (BleepingComputer, DataBreaches.net, The Record). The FBI flash alert of 11-13 describes attacks automated at machine speed.

KEV deadlines arrive tomorrow, 11-16: Check Point CVE-2026-123039 (PHP2Shell, 4 outlets), where attackers gain root on gateways and deploy a VMware ESXi wiper; and UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713 (server-level command injection).
Breaches: TSMC's employee data breach is linked to a cloud service provider (4 outlets), and a hack at a French postal unit exposed data on 22 million people.
Still active: Cursor says a stolen Fireworks AI key led to the trojanized Claude Code extension incident; Uber separately reports driver licenses stolen via Fireworks AI.

SCKit: worm-like malware aimed at MSPs that abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions; Microsoft has published details. The last 7 days score 1.23x the 90-day average.

actions: Check Point: apply the vendor fix for CVE-2026-123039 before 11-16, restrict management access, hunt for backdoors, keep ESXi backups offline.
UnrealIRCd: patch or take internet-facing servers offline for CVE-2026-114713 before 11-16, and check them for injected commands.
Read the FBI ARTEX alert and confirm patching and alerting on internet-facing systems can keep pace with automated attacks.
Cursor and Claude Code users: review installed extensions against Cursor's disclosure and rotate any Fireworks AI API keys.
ScreenConnect: inventory instances and extensions, review technician sessions and hunt for SCKit using Microsoft's guidance.
Queue Cisco BroadWorks, Openwave, Outlook and Chromium fixes before the 11-24 KEV due date.
